87|class RepeatAuth(httpx.Auth):
88|    """
89|    A mock authentication scheme that requires clients to send
90|    the request a fixed number of times, and then send a last request containing
91|    an aggregation of nonces that the server sent in 'WWW-Authenticate' headers
92|    of intermediate responses.
93|    """
94|
95|    requires_request_body = True
96|
97|    def __init__(self, repeat: int) -> None:
98|        self.repeat = repeat
99|
100|    def auth_flow(
101|        self, request: httpx.Request
102|    ) -> typing.Generator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response, None]:
103|        nonces = []
104|
105|        for index in range(self.repeat):
106|            request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Repeat {index}"
107|            response = yield request
108|            nonces.append(response.headers["www-authenticate"])
109|
110|        key = ".".join(nonces)
111|        request.headers["Authorization"] = f"Repeat {key}"
112|        yield request

115|class ResponseBodyAuth(httpx.Auth):
116|    """
117|    A mock authentication scheme that requires clients to send an 'Authorization'
118|    header, then send back the contents of the response in the 'Authorization'
119|    header.
120|    """
121|
122|    requires_response_body = True
123|
124|    def __init__(self, token: str) -> None:
125|        self.token = token

127|    def auth_flow(
128|        self, request: httpx.Request
129|    ) -> typing.Generator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response, None]:
130|        request.headers["Authorization"] = self.token
131|        response = yield request
132|        data = response.text
133|        request.headers["Authorization"] = data
134|        yield request

137|class SyncOrAsyncAuth(httpx.Auth):
138|    """
139|    A mock authentication scheme that uses a different implementation for the
140|    sync and async cases.
141|    """
142|
143|    def __init__(self) -> None:
144|        self._lock = threading.Lock()
145|        self._async_lock = anyio.Lock()
146|
147|    def sync_auth_flow(
148|        self, request: httpx.Request
149|    ) -> typing.Generator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response, None]:
150|        with self._lock:
151|            request.headers["Authorization"] = "sync-auth"
152|        yield request
153|
154|    async def async_auth_flow(
155|        self, request: httpx.Request
156|    ) -> typing.AsyncGenerator[httpx.Request, httpx.Response]:
157|        async with self._async_lock:
158|            request.headers["Authorization"] = "async-auth"
159|        yield request

232|def test_context_managed_transport():
233|    class Transport(httpx.BaseTransport):
234|        def __init__(self) -> None:
235|            self.events: list[str] = []
236|
237|        def close(self):
238|            # The base implementation of httpx.BaseTransport just
239|            # calls into `.close`, so simple transport cases can just override
240|            # this method for any cleanup, where more complex cases
241|            # might want to additionally override `__enter__`/`__exit__`.
242|            self.events.append("transport.close")
243|
244|        def __enter__(self):
245|            super().__enter__()
246|            self.events.append("transport.__enter__")
247|
248|        def __exit__(self, *args):
249|            super().__exit__(*args)
250|            self.events.append("transport.__exit__")
251|
252|    transport = Transport()
253|    with httpx.Client(transport=transport):
254|        pass
255|
256|    assert transport.events == [
257|        "transport.__enter__",
258|        "transport.close",
259|        "transport.__exit__",
260|    ]

330|async def test_cancellation_during_stream():
331|    """
332|    If any BaseException is raised during streaming the response, then the
333|    stream should be closed.
334|
335|    This includes:
336|
337|    * `asyncio.CancelledError` (A subclass of BaseException from Python 3.8 onwards.)
338|    * `trio.Cancelled`
339|    * `KeyboardInterrupt`
340|    * `SystemExit`
341|
342|    See https://github.com/encode/httpx/issues/2139
343|    """
344|    stream_was_closed = False
345|
346|    def response_with_cancel_during_stream(request):
347|        class CancelledStream(httpx.AsyncByteStream):
348|            async def __aiter__(self) -> typing.AsyncIterator[bytes]:
349|                yield b"Hello"
350|                raise KeyboardInterrupt()
351|                yield b", world"  # pragma: no cover
352|
353|            async def aclose(self) -> None:
354|                nonlocal stream_was_closed
355|                stream_was_closed = True
356|
357|        return httpx.Response(
358|            200, headers={"Content-Length": "12"}, stream=CancelledStream()
359|        )
360|
361|    transport = httpx.MockTransport(response_with_cancel_during_stream)
362|
363|    async with httpx.AsyncClient(transport=transport) as client:
364|        with pytest.raises(KeyboardInterrupt):
365|            await client.get("https://www.example.com")
366|        assert stream_was_closed

7|def url_to_origin(url: str) -> httpcore.URL:
8|    """
9|    Given a URL string, return the origin in the raw tuple format that
10|    `httpcore` uses for it's representation.
11|    """
12|    u = httpx.URL(url)
13|    return httpcore.URL(scheme=u.raw_scheme, host=u.raw_host, port=u.port, target="/")

224|class TestServer(Server):
225|    @property
226|    def url(self) -> httpx.URL:
227|        protocol = "https" if self.config.is_ssl else "http"
228|        return httpx.URL(f"{protocol}://{self.config.host}:{self.config.port}/")
229|
230|    def install_signal_handlers(self) -> None:
231|        # Disable the default installation of handlers for signals such as SIGTERM,
232|        # because it can only be done in the main thread.
233|        pass  # pragma: nocover
234|
235|    async def serve(self, sockets=None):
236|        self.restart_requested = asyncio.Event()
237|
238|        loop = asyncio.get_event_loop()
239|        tasks = {
240|            loop.create_task(super().serve(sockets=sockets)),
241|            loop.create_task(self.watch_restarts()),
242|        }
243|        await asyncio.wait(tasks)
244|
245|    async def restart(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover
246|        # This coroutine may be called from a different thread than the one the
247|        # server is running on, and from an async environment that's not asyncio.
248|        # For this reason, we use an event to coordinate with the server
249|        # instead of calling shutdown()/startup() directly, and should not make
250|        # any asyncio-specific operations.
251|        self.started = False
252|        self.restart_requested.set()
253|        while not self.started:
254|            await sleep(0.2)
255|
256|    async def watch_restarts(self) -> None:  # pragma: no cover
257|        while True:
258|            if self.should_exit:
259|                return
260|
261|            try:
262|                await asyncio.wait_for(self.restart_requested.wait(), timeout=0.1)
263|            except asyncio.TimeoutError:
264|                continue
265|
266|            self.restart_requested.clear()
267|            await self.shutdown()
268|            await self.startup()
269|
270|
271|def serve_in_thread(server: TestServer) -> typing.Iterator[TestServer]:
272|    thread = threading.Thread(target=server.run)
273|    thread.start()
274|    try:
275|        while not server.started:
276|            time.sleep(1e-3)
277|        yield server
278|    finally:
279|        server.should_exit = True
280|        thread.join()

1|# Contributing
2|
3|Thank you for being interested in contributing to HTTPX.
4|There are many ways you can contribute to the project:
5|
6|- Try HTTPX and [report bugs/issues you find](https://github.com/encode/httpx/issues/new)
7|- [Implement new features](https://github.com/encode/httpx/issues?q=is%3Aissue+is%3Aopen+label%3A%22good+first+issue%22)
8|- [Review Pull Requests of others](https://github.com/encode/httpx/pulls)
9|- Write documentation
10|- Participate in discussions
11|
12|## Reporting Bugs or Other Issues
13|
14|Found something that HTTPX should support?
15|Stumbled upon some unexpected behaviour?
16|
17|Contributions should generally start out with [a discussion](https://github.com/encode/httpx/discussions).
18|Possible bugs may be raised as a "Potential Issue" discussion, feature requests may
19|be raised as an "Ideas" discussion. We can then determine if the discussion needs
20|to be escalated into an "Issue" or not, or if we'd consider a pull request.
21|
22|Try to be more descriptive as you can and in case of a bug report,
23|provide as much information as possible like:
24|
25|- OS platform
26|- Python version
27|- Installed dependencies and versions (`python -m pip freeze`)
28|- Code snippet
29|- Error traceback
30|
31|You should always try to reduce any examples to the *simplest possible case*
32|that demonstrates the issue.
33|
34|Some possibly useful tips for narrowing down potential issues...
35|
36|- Does the issue exist on HTTP/1.1, or HTTP/2, or both?
37|- Does the issue exist with `Client`, `AsyncClient`, or both?
38|- When using `AsyncClient` does the issue exist when using `asyncio` or `trio`, or both?
39|
40|## Development
41|
42|To start developing HTTPX create a **fork** of the
43|[HTTPX repository](https://github.com/encode/httpx) on GitHub.
44|
45|Then clone your fork with the following command replacing `YOUR-USERNAME` with
46|your GitHub username:
47|
48|```shell
49|$ git clone https://github.com/YOUR-USERNAME/httpx
50|```
51|
52|You can now install the project and its dependencies using:
53|
54|```shell
55|$ cd httpx
56|$ scripts/install
57|```
58|
59|## Testing and Linting
60|
61|We use custom shell scripts to automate testing, linting,
62|and documentation building workflow.
63|
64|To run the tests, use:
65|
66|```shell
67|$ scripts/test
68|```
69|
70|!!! warning
71|    The test suite spawns testing servers on ports **8000** and **8001**.
72|    Make sure these are not in use, so the tests can run properly.
73|
74|You can run a single test script like this:
75|
76|```shell
77|$ scripts/test -- tests/test_multipart.py
78|```
79|
80|To run the code auto-formatting:
81|
82|```shell
83|$ scripts/lint
84|```
85|
86|Lastly, to run code checks separately (they are also run as part of `scripts/test`), run:
87|
88|```shell
89|$ scripts/check
90|```
91|
92|## Documenting
93|
94|Documentation pages are located under the `docs/` folder.
95|
96|To run the documentation site locally (useful for previewing changes), use:
97|
98|```shell
99|$ scripts/docs
100|```
101|
102|## Resolving Build / CI Failures
103|
104|Once you've submitted your pull request, the test suite will automatically run, and the results will show up in GitHub.
105|If the test suite fails, you'll want to click through to the "Details" link, and try to identify why the test suite failed.
106|
107|<p align="center" style="margin: 0 0 10px">
108|  <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/encode/httpx/master/docs/img/gh-actions-fail.png" alt='Failing PR commit status'>
109|</p>
110|
111|Here are some common ways the test suite can fail:
112|
113|### Check Job Failed
114|
115|<p align="center" style="margin: 0 0 10px">
116|  <img src="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/encode/httpx/master/docs/img/gh-actions-fail-check.png" alt='Failing GitHub action lint job'>
117|</p>

151|## Releasing
152|
153|*This section is targeted at HTTPX maintainers.*
154|
155|Before releasing a new version, create a pull request that includes:
156|
157|- **An update to the changelog**:
158|    - We follow the format from [keepachangelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/).
159|    - [Compare](https://github.com/encode/httpx/compare/) `master` with the tag of the latest release, and list all entries that are of interest to our users:
160|        - Things that **must** go in the changelog: added, changed, deprecated or removed features, and bug fixes.
161|        - Things that **should not** go in the changelog: changes to documentation, tests or tooling.
162|        - Try sorting entries in descending order of impact / importance.
163|        - Keep it concise and to-the-point. 🎯
164|- **A version bump**: see `__version__.py`.
165|
166|For an example, see [#1006](https://github.com/encode/httpx/pull/1006).
167|
168|Once the release PR is merged, create a
169|[new release](https://github.com/encode/httpx/releases/new) including:
170|
171|- Tag version like `0.13.3`.
172|- Release title `Version 0.13.3`
173|- Description copied from the changelog.
174|

176|

178|`scripts/publish` script.

180|## Development proxy setup
181|
182|To test and debug requests via a proxy it's best to run a proxy server locally.
183|Any server should do but HTTPCore's test suite uses
184|[`mitmproxy`](https://mitmproxy.org/) which is written in Python, it's fully
185|featured and has excellent UI and tools for introspection of requests.
186|
187|You can install `mitmproxy` using `pip install mitmproxy` or [several
188|other ways](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/overview-installation/).
189|
190|`mitmproxy` does require setting up local TLS certificates for HTTPS requests,
191|as its main purpose is to allow developers to inspect requests that pass through
192|it. We can set them up follows:
193|
194|1. [`pip install trustme-cli`](https://github.com/sethmlarson/trustme-cli/).
195|2. `trustme-cli -i example.org www.example.org`, assuming you want to test
196|connecting to that domain, this will create three files: `server.pem`,
197|`server.key` and `client.pem`.
198|3. `mitmproxy` requires a PEM file that includes the private key and the
199|certificate so we need to concatenate them:
200|`cat server.key server.pem > server.withkey.pem`.
201|4. Start the proxy server `mitmproxy --certs server.withkey.pem`, or use the
202|[other mitmproxy commands](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/) with different
203|UI options.
204|
205|At this point the server is ready to start serving requests, you'll need to
206|configure HTTPX as described in the
207|[proxy section](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/#http-proxying) and
208|the [SSL certificates section](https://www.python-httpx.org/advanced/#ssl-certificates),
209|this is where our previously generated `client.pem` comes in:
210|
211|```
212|import httpx
213|
214|ssl_context = httpx.SSLContext()
215|ssl_context.load_verify_locations("/path/to/client.pem")
216|
217|with httpx.Client(proxy="http://127.0.0.1:8080/", ssl_context=ssl_context) as client:
218|    response = client.get("https://example.org")
219|    print(response.status_code)  # should print 200
220|```
221|
222|Note, however, that HTTPS requests will only succeed to the host specified
223|in the SSL/TLS certificate we generated, HTTPS requests to other hosts will
224|raise an error like:
225|
226|```
227|ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate
228|verify failed: Hostname mismatch, certificate is not valid for
229|'duckduckgo.com'. (_ssl.c:1108)
230|```
231|
232|If you want to make requests to more hosts you'll need to regenerate the
233|certificates and include all the hosts you intend to connect to in the
234|seconds step, i.e.
235|
236|`trustme-cli -i example.org www.example.org duckduckgo.com www.duckduckgo.com`

1|# The WHATWG have various tests that can be used to validate the URL parsing.
2|#
3|# https://url.spec.whatwg.org/
4|
5|import json
6|
7|import pytest
8|
9|from httpx._urlparse import urlparse
10|
11|# URL test cases from...
12|# https://github.com/web-platform-tests/wpt/blob/master/url/resources/urltestdata.json
13|with open("tests/models/whatwg.json", "r", encoding="utf-8") as input:
14|    test_cases = json.load(input)
15|    test_cases = [
16|        item
17|        for item in test_cases
18|        if not isinstance(item, str) and not item.get("failure")
19|    ]
20|
21|
22|@pytest.mark.parametrize("test_case", test_cases)
23|def test_urlparse(test_case):
24|    if test_case["href"] in ("a: foo.com", "lolscheme:x x#x%20x"):
25|        # Skip these two test cases.
26|        # WHATWG cases where are not using percent-encoding for the space character.
27|        # Anyone know what's going on here?
28|        return
29|
30|    p = urlparse(test_case["href"])
31|
32|    # Test cases include the protocol with the trailing ":"
33|    protocol = p.scheme + ":"
34|    # Include the square brackets for IPv6 addresses.
35|    hostname = f"[{p.host}]" if ":" in p.host else p.host
36|    # The test cases use a string representation of the port.
37|    port = "" if p.port is None else str(p.port)
38|    # I have nothing to say about this one.
39|    path = p.path
40|    # The 'search' and 'hash' components in the whatwg tests are semantic, not literal.
41|    # Our parsing differentiates between no query/hash and empty-string query/hash.
42|    search = "" if p.query in (None, "") else "?" + str(p.query)
43|    hash = "" if p.fragment in (None, "") else "#" + str(p.fragment)
44|
45|    # URL hostnames are case-insensitive.
46|    # We normalize these, unlike the WHATWG test cases.
47|    assert protocol == test_case["protocol"]
48|    assert hostname.lower() == test_case["hostname"].lower()
49|    assert port == test_case["port"]
50|    assert path == test_case["pathname"]
51|    assert search == test_case["search"]
52|    assert hash == test_case["hash"]
